why: I checked all four verifier checks, and each PASS/FAIL condition tests only what its expect line's words require. Check 1 runs `--shout Ada` and passes when the greeting is "with every letter upper-cased". Its "treats `--shout` as the name" fail case follows from printing the greeting at all. Check 2 compares head with base for `Ada` and for no arguments, which is what "output is unchanged" means. Check 3 needs the file to mention `--shout` and say what it does, which is a fair reading of "documents". Check 4 can't fetch the live page before merge, so it checks the stand-in the words force: the workflow still publishes docs on pushes to main, and docs/index.md lists `--shout`. The stricter items (the `Ada --shout` order, `npm test` exiting 0, added tests, the exact output with its newline) are all under "Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL)". No check uses mutation tests, branch rules or exact-wording rules.
